brief: spokenSiteName moves out of lib/weighbridgeBoard into lib/spokenName with its tests, because it stopped being about weighbridges: the site hover card now uses it too. Display only; the geojson keeps the surveyor spelling.

The leaf counts form a column instead of a row of right-flushed numbers. Measured in a 260px rail: every count ended at 246px and began somewhere between 227.8 and 239.9, because .side-tree__rowcount had no width and "597" is 18.2px against "4" at 6.1px. Reading down a list the eye takes the LEFT edge, and a ragged one says the rows are unrelated. min-width 20px plus text-align right puts all four -- switch, link, alert-toned, and one carrying a #meta -- at left 226 / right 246; a fourth digit widens the box to 24.2px rather than clipping. Also dropped flex-wrap from .side-tree__row--link: the second line it wrapped onto was .side-tree__rownote, deleted earlier today, so all it could still do was drop a count below a long label.

The scale names under Quick line read as far larger than the rows above them, and the font size was never the reason: they are the same .side-tree__row at 12.5px that Movement uses. The provider sends centre names in capitals -- OPAPO, NAITIRI, WESTERN MILL -- and capitals at a matched size do not read as a matched size. New spokenSiteName in lib/weighbridgeBoard lowers a word only when it is entirely capitals, so a name that already arrives in mixed case is left as somebody meant it, and digits are never inside a match so a code beside the name survives. Display only: buildBoard keeps the provider spelling, which is what a ticket and a CSV have to match, and its tests still assert WESTERN MILL. Four tests added, 746 -> 750.

The scales branch under Map layers is called "Quick line" instead of "Weighbridges". Two labels carry it: the TreeNode heading in the sidebar, and the layer object built in FleetMap, which is what the map's own layers popover prints and what the branch title "Draw <label> on the map" is built from. Label only -- the layer id, the hook, the API and the Weighbridges SCREEN in the footer nav are untouched, so nothing that reads prefs or routes by name has moved.

FOCUS_ZOOM goes 20 -> 17, which is every camera move to a single vehicle: marker clicks, the header search, live-feed notifications, the stranded window, the pinned-unit zoom, and the new Units-list tick. 20 framed the vehicle and nothing else, answering "which pixel" rather than "what is this unit doing". It was raised from 17 on 2026-08-05 to chase a new maxZoom of 21 -- and the raise was never carried into the comments: FIT_MAX_ZOOM's note still read "that is what FOCUS_ZOOM 17 is for", and FOCUS_EXIT_ZOOM still described 14 as "three steps below FOCUS_ZOOM", true at 17 and six steps out at 20. Both are accurate again. TRACK_FOCUS_ZOOM, added an hour earlier to give the tick 17 while the shared constant stayed 20, is deleted rather than left as a second name for the same number. BRIDGE_FOCUS_ZOOM now equals FOCUS_ZOOM and is kept separate anyway -- a scale is a place with a yard and a vehicle is a thing on a road, and they will not want retuning on the same day.

Unticking a box zooms back out. Every untick, not only the one that empties the set: unticking is the reader saying they are done with that unit, and the close-up the tick bought them is the first thing that stops being useful. Keyed on the tracked COUNT falling rather than on the tick handler, so all three ways out land here -- the row tick, the header select-all, and the Tracking-N chip clear. The destination is the view saved on the way IN, captured once so a second tick cannot overwrite it with the first unit close-up; it survives until the set is actually empty, so a second and third untick go back to the same place rather than to wherever the last one left off. Guards: the view is null until a tick has moved the camera, making this a no-op on mount, and it carries the org that made it -- switching organisation also empties the set, and Sukari and Mufindi are a border apart, so a mismatched view is dropped rather than flown to. Zoom level for the tick is TRACK_FOCUS_ZOOM at 17, its own constant beside BRIDGE_FOCUS_ZOOM rather than a change to FOCUS_ZOOM: 20 is for a focus that isolates one unit deliberately without context, and is still what marker clicks, header search, feed notifications and the stranded window use. Watching a lorry means seeing the road it is on.

Ticking a unit in the Units list now takes the camera to it. Ticking already narrowed the map and opened the unit's detail panel, but left the reader to find the thing they had just asked to watch among 596 others. New handleZoomUnit in FleetMap rather than the existing handleFocusVehicle: that one calls setFocusedId, and isolating the map to a single unit is the opposite of what a tick means -- the second tick would erase the first. It pans, sets FOCUS_ZOOM, and claims the pending fit so the fleet-wide fit cannot pull the camera back out. No feed narrowing and no search halo: those both say 'this is the subject', where a tick says only 'include this one'. On the way in only -- moving the camera on an UNtick would send the reader somewhere they did not ask to go, with nothing ticked to have gone there for. Select-all goes through toggleAllShown, which bypasses this, so ticking twenty units does not try to fly to one.

Every element carrying a note class comes off, across 24 files -- 51 in all, including two built as HTML strings inside FleetMap rather than as JSX. This goes past the standing-rule prose removed earlier: it takes live figures with it (stop counts and coordinates, km-remaining on the maintenance card, warehouse tallies), loading and error lines in route playback, the layer-loading status in the map-layers menu, and the repair history's per-step comments. One survivor: the About-the-trip textarea in RepairReportForm, whose class is a field modifier rather than a note -- its value is submitted to the API and gates the form's dirty check, so removing it would silently drop data. Three locals (replaced, serviced, hasPassword) and two TreeLink/TableToolbar props lost their only readers and went with them. Dead CSS left in place: the rules are invisible and an automated sweep mangled comment blocks.
files: 24 files under src/components/ -- see git diff

brief: The last two TreeNotes come off the sidebar, and TreeNote with them. One was the site-plans line naming which plan was still fetching; the other, under the fleet-type filter, read "Nothing ticked means the whole fleet, not an empty map." The second is the same species as the stopped-in-transit footnote and the weighbridge instruction already removed: a rule in prose, parked under the controls it describes, read once and then read past forever. The first was a live status rather than a rule, which is why it was kept a turn ago -- but a status that costs a whole row in a rail short of vertical room, to say a word the row itself could carry, does not earn the space either. With no call sites left, the TreeNote component and its .side-tree__note rule are dead and go too.

The standing instruction under the list of scales — "Clicking a scale takes the map to it. Hover its marker for the last ticket; click to keep the card open." — comes off, the same call as the stopped-in-transit footnote and for the same reason: it is documentation parked inside a control, read once and then read past forever, in a rail whose rows are already short of vertical room. The first sentence was redundant on arrival — every scale row carries a title reading "Take the map to <centre> bridge <n>", which says it at the moment it is wanted instead of permanently. The site-plans TreeNote two branches up STAYS: it names which plan is still fetching, which is a live status rather than a rule, and it disappears by itself when the answer changes.

Every flagged row now says WHERE, on a line of its own under the plate — the one fact of the three that cannot be got by looking at the map, since a stranded unit is by definition outside every place the estate has a name for. Through usePlaceName, the hook the vehicle card and the map overlay already use, so the coordinate fallback and the per-cell cache are the same ones; the row became a component because a hook cannot be called per row from the parent. Paging paid for this: ten lookups a page instead of one per flagged unit. "Location unverified" is retired in both panels — printed under a place name it reads as doubt about the name, which it never meant; it is about zones, and now says so. The row was tightened rather than allowed to grow (55px, three lines set 1.25) and the ceiling raised to the measured 650 a full page needs; below a ~930px viewport a page of ten scrolls, which is the right trade.

Ten units a page, on the roster's own paginate/pageWindow rather than a slice written here — the hard part is not the slice, it is clamping a page against a list that shrinks while somebody is reading it, which on this panel is the ordinary case and is already solved and tested in lib/rosterView. The pager is the accounts table's, at a window's scale: range left, steps and numbers right, no rows-per-page because a 320px window has nothing to spend a choice on. It wraps where the table's does not need to, so a three-digit page count drops the nav to its own line instead of pushing the close button off the panel. Page resets when the window is REOPENED, never when the data changes — a pager that jumps home on every telemetry sweep cannot be read — and the list scrolls back to its top on a page change. Track all still means every flagged unit, not the visible ten, because the count it sits beside says so; the deliberate opposite of the roster's select-all, which means the page.

The rule-of-the-flag footnote — "Moving, then stationary 10 min or more, outside every known zone" — comes off both surfaces that carried it, the map window and the fleets menu's flagged list. It was documentation sitting permanently inside an operating panel: read once, then re-read past every time the list is opened, on a panel whose whole job is six plates and how long each has been standing. The rows already say the part that changes — the duration, engine running or off, and "location unverified" when the zone pass has not reached that unit. The definition does not change, so it does not belong on a panel that is opened to see what has. The empty state keeps its sentence, which is an answer rather than a definition.

public/oyani-site.geojson re-cut from the operations team's fresh Google Earth export, through tools/kml-to-site.mjs rather than by hand, so the ring is the surveyor's and the categorisation is the same pass every other survey went through. The old outline was 1.7 km south-east of the real yard and 1.01 ha against its 0.75 — not a drift, a different piece of ground, which means every guest-occupancy answer this layer has ever given for Oyani was about somewhere else. The gate keeps the name the survey gives it, Main Gate, and lands inside the fence on the converter's own containment check. The figures the site-plan table states in prose — the hectares, and the 32 km / 13 km spread that justifies three switches instead of one Sukari layer — are re-measured from the new ring rather than left to describe the old one.

The tree's section titles (MAP LAYERS, FLEETS) take the stat captions' weight and tracking — 500/0.05em, not 700/0.07em — finishing the rail's alignment; size follows too, 11px to 10 — two uppercase labels a pixel apart read as an error rather than as a rank, and there is no rank to say between FLEETS and MOVING. The stranded window now dismisses on a press outside as well as Escape and its close button, on pointerdown in the capture phase, the same contract the Units panel and the map's menus use.

theme: in-project (the app's light surface, the Units window's geometry)
brief: Stopped in transit moves inside the sidebar's Movement branch and stops being a list there: it is now a link that opens StrandedWindow over the map, the same arrangement Units already has, because every row in that list is an instruction to look at a place. Each row carries the Units panel's own tick, writing the same trackedIds, so the map can be narrowed to the stranded units; the branch keeps a red dot while it is shut so the alarm survives being folded away.

The tree branch labels — Site plans, Weighbridges, Machine types, Movement — take the nav's ink (#475569) instead of #334155, and one weight step instead of two (500, not 600). They were the darkest and heaviest text in the rail, sitting directly under the page links at #475569/400: two lists in one panel with the less important one shouting.

The window's list takes the Units panel's scrollbar — `scrollbar-width: thin`, and nothing else. It was on the platform default, measured at 15px against the Units list's 10 beside it; two windows that open from the same rail and scroll the same kind of list must not scroll differently.

theme: studied-DNA (image reference; in-project Inter + sp4 scale preserved, light only)
brief: User accounts redesign toward a supplied admin-roster screenshot: titled masthead + count badge, split toolbar, Table/Board/List views, avatar identity column, status as a dot, bulk select, column chooser, CSV export, pagination, undo toast; dark token layer removed (app is light-only)

The invite band becomes a modal right-hand panel on the live map's vehicle-panel shape: portalled to body, scrim, scrolling body with the actions on a fixed foot, Escape in capture so it does not also leave the page, focus trapped and returned to the trigger. The error/notice pair moved out of the form onto the page, where the roster's own messages could finally be seen.

Roster: Email and Phone become their own columns and leave the name cell; Roles here -> Roles; status returns to a badge with the dot kept inside it; Edit access becomes Edit and opens the whole person in the same right-hand panel as Add user - details (PATCH against their home organisation), account state with Suspend/Reactivate, and access. Two latent bugs fixed on the way: a 180px min-width meant for the name cell that the new checkbox column had inherited, and a delete-confirmation colSpan still counting six fixed columns.

Sized for a tenant with twenty organisations: held organisations listed, the rest behind one counted control with a filter past eight, roles expanded one at a time with their chips acting as the control. One component now serves both panels. Roles are fetched for what is on screen instead of for every organisation the admin can reach.

Title, count badge and strapline replaced by two state badges - N active, N suspended - in the Status column's own voice, plus an 'N of M shown' caveat while a filter is on. The <h1> is visually hidden rather than removed, because the page's only other name is a breadcrumb <li>.

Email and Phone are masked in the roster (domain kept, last three digits kept, length never revealed) and revealed per person by clicking the masked value itself, which then becomes a real mailto/tel link. Search, CSV export and the profile panel still carry the full value. Role chips deduplicate on the role name, so a role granted twice is listed once.

One row per person rather than one per membership, with organisations shown as badges carrying each tenant's mark and roles unioned across them; Delete is withheld on a merged row. Contact masking becomes a toolbar switch over the per-person reveal. Pager arrows, the range dash, the page ellipsis and the toast close were printing their own \\uXXXX source in JSX text and are now drawn or escaped properly. The board and list views get the scroller only the table had, so their last rows are reachable.

Masking is reversible and per field. Email and phone switch independently on each row; the masked value is the button that reveals it, and a revealed value keeps its mailto/tel link with a three-dot control beside it that puts the mask back. Per-cell state is held as exceptions to the toolbar switch, so one control reads correctly in both directions.

Cards drag between Active and Suspended to change an account, with the derived columns (Pending, No live invite) refusing a drop rather than accepting one and doing nothing. The gesture is stated above the board together with its keyboard equivalent, a card cannot be dragged by its own owner, and handleStatus now takes a destination rather than flipping.
Kanban cards list every organisation the person holds, as badges with their marks, no longer gated on the table's column-visibility flag and no longer capped or scrolled the way the grid cell is.

List rows carry the same organisation badges, between the person and their state, shrinkable to 42% of the row; under 768px the names are clipped to visually-hidden and the marks alone carry it, with title restoring the name to a pointer.

Suspend/Reactivate inside the profile panel is now staged rather than immediate: it marks the account, the badge shows the draft, a note states what Save will do, and Cancel or closing the panel discards it. The status write runs last in the save, after the membership removals, because it is the one call that can end the session making the others. Row-level and board gestures stay immediate.

Account events - created, invited, re-invited, suspended, reactivated, profile saved, deleted - report through the undo toast instead of the page message strip, with an undo on single suspend/reactivate and none drawn where there is nothing to undo. The strip keeps errors and the two messages that describe a standing problem rather than an event.

Bulk suspend, reactivate and resend report through the toast, with the undo handed to runBulk rather than raised beside it - which also removes a double report whose two counts disagreed. Partial results stay on the page and carry no undo.

Errors and standing problems report in the toast too, and the page's message strip is removed. Three tones - outcome, standing problem, failure - where the tone decides whether the message is on a nine-second clock; only outcomes expire. Colour is backed by a left rule and a mark, and a failure is announced assertively. Drawers keep their inline error beside the submit button.

Toast moves to the bottom right, on the side the page's own actions are, and is colour-coded by operation rather than by mood: created, reactivated/saved, suspended, deleted, standing problem and failure each carry their own rule colour and their own mark, with the mark rather than the hue separating the pairs that share one.

The Organisations list in the account panel names each tenant by its logo mark as well as its name, the same device the roster's Organisation column already uses; the mark is lifted into its own OrgMark component so both draw one thing, sized 18px for the panel's bolder row, with the hued letter fallback kept for tenants with no artwork.

The account page names organisations by their logo marks in both places it lists them — the overview chips and the Access tab — replacing an initials disc that merely abbreviated the name sitting beside it; one 20px box carries either the artwork or, where there is none, the initials it replaced.

The hued avatar and the pager are deliberately not taken — this row already spends four colours on meaning, and the ranked roster grows rather than pages.

Both themes, every width: the window reads the app greys instead of this file second :root (2.05 dark / 2.56 light), the chips get a real colour-mix tint instead of the dropped var()22 string, one label voice replaces three, micro step 9.5 to 11px
